name: Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Cook spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until al dente.
In a bowl, whisk together eggs and grated Parmesan cheese. Season with black pepper.
Fry pancetta with garlic in a pan over medium heat until crispy.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta cooking water before draining.
Remove pan from heat. Add drained pasta to the pancetta.
Quickly pour the egg-cheese mixture over pasta, tossing continuously.
Add pasta water a little at a time to create a creamy sauce.
Serve immediately with extra Parmesan and black pepper.
cooking_tips: Never add cream — the creaminess comes from eggs and pasta water.
Remove the pan from heat before adding eggs to prevent scrambling.
Use guanciale (cured pork cheek) for the most authentic version.
serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with extra Parmesan and a simple green salad.
storage_tips: Best eaten fresh. Can be refrigerated for 1 day but sauce may dry out.

name: Margherita Pizza
instructions: Preheat oven to 250°C (480°F) with a pizza stone or baking sheet inside.
Stretch pizza dough on a floured surface to desired thickness.
Spread tomato sauce evenly, leaving a border for the crust.
Tear mozzarella and distribute over the sauce.
Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until crust is golden and cheese is bubbly.
Remove from oven and immediately top with fresh basil leaves.
Drizzle with more olive oil and serve immediately.
cooking_tips: A very hot oven is key to a good pizza crust.
Don't overload with toppings — less is more for Margherita.
Add fresh basil after baking to preserve its flavor.
serving_suggestions: Serve hot, cut into slices. Pair with a simple arugula salad.
storage_tips: Best eaten fresh. Reheat in oven at 200°C for 5 minutes.

substitutions.pizza dough: flatbread or tortilla for quick version

name: Risotto ai Funghi
instructions: Heat vegetable broth in a saucepan and keep warm.
Sauté mushrooms in olive oil until golden. Season and set aside.
In another pan, sweat onions and garlic in butter until soft.
Add arborio rice and toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in white wine and stir until absorbed.
Add warm broth one ladle at a time, stirring constantly until absorbed.
Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Stir in mushrooms, Parmesan, and remaining butter. Season to taste.
cooking_tips: Never stop stirring — it releases the starch that makes risotto creamy.
The final addition of butter and cheese (mantecatura) is what makes it silky.
serving_suggestions: Serve immediately in warmed bowls. Garnish with truffle oil for luxury.
storage_tips: Risotto doesn't store well. Best made and eaten immediately.

name: Chicken Piccata
instructions: Pound chicken breasts thin between plastic wrap.
Season with salt and pepper and dredge in flour, shake off excess.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook chicken 3 minutes per side until golden. Transfer to plate.
In the same pan, sauté garlic briefly.
Add white wine and chicken broth, scraping up any brown bits.
Add lemon juice, capers, and butter. Simmer until sauce thickens.
Return chicken to sauce, simmer 2 minutes, garnish with parsley.
cooking_tips: Don't skip the flour — it helps create the sauce.
Use fresh lemon juice for bright, fresh flavor.
serving_suggestions: Serve over angel hair pasta or with roasted vegetables.
storage_tips: Refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat gently to avoid drying out.

name: Penne Arrabbiata
instructions: Cook penne in salted boiling water until al dente.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add sliced garlic and red chili flakes. Cook until garlic is fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, salt, and a pinch of sugar.
Simmer sauce for 15 minutes until thickened.
Toss drained pasta with the sauce.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve hot.
cooking_tips: Arrabbiata means 'angry' in Italian — make it as spicy as you like.
Save pasta water to adjust sauce consistency.
Use San Marzano tomatoes for best flavor.
serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread and a green salad.
storage_tips: Sauce keeps for 3 days. Cook pasta fresh when serving.
